title: Introduction to Generics knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Introduction to Generics”?
options: It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
Generics preserve relationships between types and reduce unsafe casts; type constraints and variance should be as simple as the API requires.
questions.answer_key: Generics preserve relationships between types and reduce unsafe casts; type constraints and variance should be as simple as the API requires.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: Generics preserve relationships between types and reduce unsafe casts; type constraints and variance should be as simple as the API requires. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Introduction to Generics”?
options: Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Introduction to Generics”?
options: Treat draft or experimental features as universally stable.
Introduction to Generics removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
Expose every internal implementation detail to every caller.
Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
questions.answer_key: Introduction to Generics removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.explanation: The misconception to avoid is: Introduction to Generics removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.
